item.title: Tinnitus Is Connected to Sleep
item.description:
📝 The Oxford researchers proposed that the large spontaneous waves of brain activity that occur during deep sleep, or non-rapid eye movement sleep (non-REM), might suppress the brain activity that leads to tinnitus. In experiments published in 2024, researchers found that ferrets that developed more severe tinnitus also showed disrupted sleep. " Crucially, the ferrets that developed tinnitus showed overly responsive brain activity to sound.
🔗 Read more: https://www.sciencealert.com/tinnitus-is-somehow-connected-to-a-crucial-bodily-function
